head: 4ea4a824
headSubject: feat(SEC-3): live-fire the Linux plugin cgroup ceiling in Docker, close SEC-3
summary: Implemented the full SEC-3/QUAL-49/QUAL-50 plan across three tracks, all committed and pushed to origin/main (866c4fb1..4ea4a824). Track C (QUAL-50) triaged 5 security-sweep hits and fixed QUAL-46's guard. Track B (QUAL-49) root-caused the runtime-surface-evidence red to a -PendingOk invocation mismatch plus one real regression, and inverted the retired-checks default so it cannot recur. Track A (SEC-3) live-fired the Linux cgroup plugin ceiling in Docker for the first time, confirming and fixing the predicted child-cgroup-nesting defect, then catching two further unanticipated defects via the live-fire itself: swap absorption defeating the OOM kill (fixed, memory.swap.max=0) and a Windows Job Object startup-commit failure at 256MB on this machine (reverted that one test to its previously-verified 128MB rather than chase a JVM-tuning fix, filed as QUAL-51).
nextStep: Two new follow-up items were filed and are the natural next work, neither blocking: (1) QUAL-51 (ledger/items/QUAL-51.yml) -- root-cause which HotSpot subsystem's commit crosses a tight OS memory ceiling on child JVM boot (PluginIpcChildProcess.spawn() passes no -Xmx/-Xms at all), fix by passing explicit conservative JVM memory flags when limits.memoryLimitMb() is set, then re-raise PluginIpcChildProcessWindowsResourceLimitTest back to 256MB with both its tests passing reliably across multiple runs. (2) SEC-4 (ledger/items/SEC-4.yml) -- a design decision, not a bugfix: whether/how to wire real generated-app java-source plugin capability calls through PluginIpcChildProcessPool for production traffic (today only test harnesses exercise it); read its own two open design questions before writing any code. Neither has a deadline; pick whichever the user prioritizes.
verified: Track C: run-all-gates.ps1 -Only aiKnowledge green (40/40 checks, 0 blocking findings). Track B: run-all-gates.ps1 -Only runtimeHost green. Track A: scripts/quality/run-linux-plugin-resource-proof.ps1 -Force passed live in Docker (3/3 JUnit tests, canCreateSiblingWithMemoryMax=true); full run-all-gates.ps1 (all four T2 gates: generator, runtimeHost, kernel, aiKnowledge) green as the final verification after the Windows-test revert. All three commits pushed to origin/main.
